machine.shared: A development machine, with other work running at times; the A/B runs are alternated for that reason

build.tls: OpenSSL 3.6.3 (bundled, static); mbedTLS not built on this machine
build.note: CONFIG_DEBUG_TRACK_MEMORY is on (the .config of this machine): every allocation is tracked. A build without it does less work per allocation; that build was not measured here.

method.ab: 7.25.20 and 7.25.21 each built from their own tree: a git worktree of the 7.25.20 tag with the same .config and compiler, where only the kernel libraries, modules/c/test, the benchmarks of performance/c/ and the three ctest binaries were built. outputs_ext was shared between the two trees: linux-ext-libs moved from 1.22 to 1.23 in this release, but the change is only how openresty is downloaded, and no library changed version, so both sides link the same external libraries. Measured: the benchmarks of performance/c/ and the ctest binaries test_topic_pkey_integer, test_topic_pkey_integer_iterator2 and test_topic_pkey_integer_iterator5. The two binaries of each benchmark run alternately, the order flipped every round, with a sync and a 3 s pause before each run: 8 rounds, 24 for the three ctest binaries. Mean +- standard deviation (median). No module was padded or relinked: a whole-release build also moves where the code lands, so a change of a few percent is not told apart from placement.
method.tag_run: The benchmarks of performance/c/ on the build of 7.25.21, 5 rounds run after the A/B run, with a sync and a 3 s pause before each run, no CPU pinning. The appends and reads of the three ctest binaries are the 7.25.21 side of the A/B run (24 rounds). The per-second benchmarks drop their first and last second; reads page by page are the FORWARD pass.

story.title: Yuneta 7.25.21: secrets masked everywhere, and nothing slower
story.lead: 7.25.21 is a security and correctness release. Credentials are masked in every trace, every kw the kernel dumps, the traffic dumps and `view-config`; a gbuffer can be marked secret (hidden from the dumps, wiped when it is freed); `C_TCP` and `C_TCP_S` stop and start again cleanly and count their connections; the rt_disk feeds of timeranger2 hear every delete. None of it is on the paths that run every second at the default trace levels: the masking runs only when a trace prints. Measured against 7.25.20 on the same machine, each release built from its own tree, the two run alternately: no figure is slower beyond the spread of its rounds, and no figure is claimed faster either.

hero.text: figures slower than 7.25.20 beyond their spread, out of the 32 measured. The secret masking is paid only when a trace prints. On the paths that run every second, a secret gbuffer costs the test of one flag, and a TCP send one key lookup.

tiles: treedb: update a node and save it
TLS echo through the gobj stack
story.append_note: same as 7.25.20 (223,031; +1.3%, inside the spread), 24 alternated rounds
story.ab_sub: Each benchmark built twice, from the tree of each release, and the two binaries run alternately: 8 rounds, 24 for the three timeranger2 tests. A change inside its whisker is noise. Everything is on one axis: the change of the time an operation takes.
story.prices_sub: What got slower, how much, and what it buys.
story.no_prices: None. No figure of 7.25.21 is slower than 7.25.20 beyond the spread of its rounds. Three moved outside it, all of them faster, and none is claimed as a gain: the TCP echo through the gobj stack (+4.8% round trips), the BFF logins (+3.1%) and 600 000 appends to one key (-3.7% of time). No change of this release takes work off those paths (a TCP send gained a key lookup), the append code is the same as in 7.25.20, and the same append benchmark moved +3.6% the other way in the last report. Both releases are built whole, so the code lands at other addresses: that is placement, not speed.
